validator_result: OK. The validator reports no errors. Only expected warnings remain: source_units is out of date for overclock-self, execute-target and disable-machine (the merge pass runs sync-patterns), dash is still a planned pattern, and the unit links tempest-rising.dynasty.matchstick and tempest-rising.dynasty.machinist point to units not researched yet. Three ATYPICAL lines apply to these units, and each is recorded in that unit's atypical list under its exact rule string, with a note: 'weapon-families:tesla allowed.damage-types armour-piercing' (Voltaic Tank, armament/0/family), and 'weapon-families:blades allowed.damage-types explosive' and 'weapon-families:blades allowed.weapon-delivery ram' (Tempest Sphere, armament/0/family).
copy_check_result: Exit 0 ("OK: no shared runs") for the copy-check run with --only on the wiki's pages and on the game's Steam news posts. It checked 13 cited pages, all from the cache, and could not check none. The first run found 2 shared runs, which I rewrote. I also ran an extra check of my prose against all 108 cached Tempest Rising wiki and Steam pages I read, cited or not, taking each Steam post's text from the page's embedded post data. It found 2 more runs, which I also rewrote. Only matches of URL strings inside uncertain notes remain. No PDF was cited.

hesitations.reason: The roles rule lets a word form name a role (harasses for harasser), so I read the build tooltip's 'Attack disables targeted buildings' as naming disabler, which then ranks at secondary step 1. The batch registry note's list of role words found in these tooltips does not include it. Read the other way, both roles rank at step 3 and list order puts anti-infantry first.

If 'disables' names disabler, step 1 has two roles and must use the bonus test. Anti-armour wins only through Voltaic Reaction, a status-tied bonus against armour (registry note). Without that bonus, step 1 would 'go on', and an anti label is not strength wording, so step 5 would give assault. The bonus itself is contested, because the Tempest Overflow page leaves the tank out of its Voltaic Reaction list. If 'disables' does not name a role, anti-armour wins at step 1 outright.

The rule is clear: a splash weapon gives anti-infantry, and no official text calls infantry a weak point. But the wiki's own Unit page says infantry resist Cannon damage, so the role may not describe the tank well.

The sources call it a charged particle beam whose attack arcs to nearby targets, so tesla fits by behaviour (electric arcs that jump). Prism needs light that splits, plasma needs travelling bolts, and laser does not arc. The registry note says only that Voltaic weapons are not lasers.
The source says 'beam', but the charge builds before the shot, not while the beam stays on the target. No source says how the shot travels, so I used the family default.

alternatives: chain only or splash only (the arcs may be the visible form of the area damage)
stun or root plus silence for the building shutdown
hesitations.reason: The splash rule is met by the area-of-effect figure and the tooltip, and chain by the prose 'arcs to nearby targets'. For powered-down buildings: silence means 'can't fire', a structure cannot move, and no source says the stop is very short, so silence over stun. I left out charge-up because its coding rule needs a held trigger and the wind-up is automatic.

alternatives: execute-target only (silence trait alone for the shutdown)
hesitations.reason: disable-machine names turrets among the machines it stops, but Structural Overload works only on buildings, never on vehicles. It is a partial fit, so I recorded it in uncertain.
The tooltip calls the cannon long-ranged, but its reach is about 1.28 times the reference rifle's. Figures decide when both have them.
The page calls it ineffective against structures, but weak damage still counts, and it does attack buildings in order to power them down.
No source text says where the gun sits. I followed the tank designation and the tie-break's classic-tank reading. The source is unclear, not the rule.
The registry note says to treat the Martial Plan as a side-wide effect, so the commander-power reading applies. The rule was clear once the note settled it.

hesitations.chosen: toggle (one entry for Tempest Dynamos / Safe Firing)
hesitations.reason: The two buttons undo each other, so they are one entry, and the tank can move in both states. Both directions have the same 30-second cooldown, which bands medium.

alternatives: no immune:crush, if the 1.6.0 fix changed the vehicle type
hesitations.reason: Patch 1.6.0 fixed a display bug that labelled its unit type 'Harvester' on the armour tab. The Unit and Crushing pages still class it as Heavy vehicle (Harvester), and no source says the crush rules changed. I treated the fix as display only.

hesitations.chosen: damage:armour-piercing, role:scout and role:anti-air as reasoned entries
hesitations.reason: The matchups rule allows reasoned entries that name their facts (infobox resistances, sight shorter than reach, a Ground-only weapon) with an uncertain note. Whether they add enough to keep is a judgement call.
No damage type, trait or pattern names units that build Tempest Charge, so matchups rule 3 lets the unit links stand alone. I also added a fit_note.

Official text was read (the build tooltip copy, the showcase post, the 1.6.0 notes). The Tempest Overflow page conflicts on a point that decides a pattern link and, under my disabler reading, the step-1 bonus test. Under the high-or-medium tie-break the conflict does not decide a coded term, but that is debatable.

I read the Codex sentence saying tanks, infantry and even walls cannot stand up to the Sphere as official strength wording. The registry note says to read the Codex like a manual paragraph, but its phrase list does not include 'no match for'. Anti-armour, named first, fails its requires (explosive damage, no infest pattern), so step 4 gives anti-infantry. If the sentence does not count, step 5 gives assault.
Assault comes in at step 4 (heavier armour, short main weapon). Anti-armour and a base-breaker role fit but cannot be claimed, so they are recorded in fit_notes.
There is no term for a rolling ball (the game's movetype is Roller). Wheels, as one big wheel, is the nearest; recorded as a gap.
Steer is the default for wheels, and no Handling tie-break reason applies. The Codex's 'somewhat ponderous' is momentum, which goes in notes only.
No body plan describes a sphere. Casemate (no turret, attacks straight ahead, body aim) breaks no rule. Disc has the round shape but is only for fliers and hovercraft. Recorded as a gap.

No footprint source exists. The stand-in in the sizes rule (its Heavy vehicle crush group is above the tank's Medium group) shows it is bigger than a tank but not that it is twice the size, and the rule gives no outcome for a bigger group. The registry note's 'biggest units ... super-heavy by size' points to huge.
Check A lets the registry note make it super-heavy, and the note lifts the Sphere 'by size'. With the size coded large, super-heavy rests on the note alone.

hesitations.chosen: flat-pool plus a passive Tempest Plating ability with empty patterns
hesitations.reason: The abilities rule says to use a word-list term when it says the same thing. Self-repair is healing on its own, while Plating heals only by using up a debuff (Tempest Charge). The registry note says to record Plating but not how.

alternatives: explosives (allows ram and explosive damage with no atypical)
hesitations.reason: The family follows behaviour. The roller is a kinetic body slam (closest to a hammer), not a charge that explodes. No ram family exists, so two atypicals and a fit_note follow.
The sources describe the Sphere slamming itself into targets, and ram comes before melee in the delivery order.

alternatives: short (the figure is about a tenth of the rifle's reach)
hesitations.reason: The blow lands at touching distance, which the melee-or-short tie-break sends to melee.

alternatives: ground-vehicle and structure only (infantry are crushed by the mobility trait, not slammed)
hesitations.reason: The wiki's weapon box says the roller hits what is too big to crush. The 1.7.0 notes speak of 'attack targets it cannot crush', which implies its attack also covers crushable targets. The rules do not say whether a kill by crushing counts as the weapon hitting.
Vulnerability (extra damage taken from every source) matches only half of mark, which also reveals the target. Recorded as a gap.
The abilities rule sends a speed-only boost with no other cost to dash, but this charge also crushes and slams along its line. I linked dash, the trait's key pattern, and added a fit_note.

A Demolitionist appears and fights on, but it is a full tier 3 heavy infantry unit, not basic crew with low health. No source says it is the pilot or that it can take a new vehicle (which pilot-eject needs). Recorded as a gap.
The Codex says 'tanks', which the rule codes as class:vehicle. The link is false for heavy vehicles and hover units, but those are a minority, so it stays.
These rest on infobox resistances, the showcase's weakness to air and Vulnerability's effect. Each has an uncertain note saying it is reasoned.

unclear_rules.topic: Verb forms in a role line
unclear_rules.note: The roles rule lets 'any word form' of a label name a role (harasses for harasser), but the batch registry note's list of role words in Tempest Rising tooltips leaves out the Voltaic Tank's 'disables targeted buildings'. If 'disables' names disabler, step 1 has two roles, and the result then depends on the step-1 bonus test, which here rests on a status-tied, contested bonus (Voltaic Reaction). A ruling would settle both the primary path and the order of the secondary roles.

The registry note lists phrases that give strengths (good against, devastates, tears apart...) and says to read the Codex like a manual paragraph, but does not say whether the list is complete. The Sphere's Codex says tanks, infantry and walls are 'no match for' it, and that alone decides anti-infantry versus assault as its primary role.

unclear_rules.topic: Size when the game's size group is larger than the tank's
unclear_rules.note: The sizes rule's stand-in names outcomes only for a group 'about the same' as the tank's (large) or smaller (medium), not for a bigger group without a twice-the-size figure. The registry note lifts the Sphere to super-heavy 'by size', which suggests huge, but gives no footprint.
For a unit whose attack order crushes smaller targets (a mobility trait) and slams bigger ones with its weapon, the rules do not say whether the crushed kinds belong in the weapon's can_target.
The charge-up coding rule needs the player to hold the trigger, which never happens in an RTS, so an automatic wind-up before every shot, a real telegraph, has no home.
disable-machine's summary covers machines including turrets, but nothing says whether a weapon that powers down any building (and never vehicles) should link it, or rely on the silence trait alone.

The abilities rule says to use a term when it 'says the same', but self-repair only partly matches a perk that heals by using up a debuff. The registry note says to record Tempest Plating without saying as what.

The on-death terms have no outcome for a vehicle whose death leaves a full combat unit, as opposed to basic crew or a pilot who can take a new vehicle. The Pillager (spawns an Ignitor) will meet the same question.

The copy-check's HTML-to-text step drops tag attributes, and Steam news pages keep the post body (and the og:description) only inside attributes. The official copy-check therefore compares prose against almost none of a Steam post's text and passes trivially. My extra check, which parsed the embedded post data, found a real 6-word run from the 1.6.0 notes that the official check missed.

new_mechanics.summary: A passive that uses up harmful stacks put on the unit by enemies or the ground (here Tempest Charge, which slows vehicles) to repair it, so a debuff meant to cripple it heals it instead, though being pushed into the debuff's capped end state (Overflow) still hurts it faster than it heals. Counterplay: don't feed it the debuff and use plain damage, or burst it straight into the capped state with weapons that inflict it directly.

source_problems:
1. The Tempest Overflow page's 'Voltaic Reaction' box lists only the Tempest Instability Missile and the Sniper. That is a word-for-word copy of the Overflow passive's list just above it, and it leaves out the Voltaic Tank, Operative, Machinist and Voltaic Railgun, which the Ability page lists. I settled this in favour of the Voltaic Tank page (infobox weapon passive, weapon box and prose) and the Ability page, and recorded it in uncertain with sources_disagree.
2. Page staleness. The Voltaic Tank page is verified only at 1.6.0+53407, the Tempest Sphere page at 1.7.0+55422 and the Machine Shop page (which carries the build tooltips) at 1.2.0+46253. I checked every patch page and the official notes from 1.6.0 through 2.0.1. The later notes hold no value changes for either unit; only two Sphere bug fixes, in 1.8.0 and 1.9.0, which I recorded.
3. Patch 1.6.0 fixed a UI issue that showed 'Harvester' as the Voltaic Tank's unit type in its armour tab. The Unit and Crushing pages still class it as Heavy vehicle (Harvester), uncrushable, so it is unclear whether only the label changed.
4. The Status effect page's Vulnerability entry leaves out the Tempest Sphere, which the Sphere page, the Ability page and the 1.7.0 notes all give it. Its Tempest Charge entry also leaves out the Matchstick and Machinist, which the Ability and Tempest Charge pages list.
5. Each of the two pre-launch showcase posts has one line of text plus a video, which I did not watch.
6. Steam news pages keep the post body only inside an HTML data attribute, so the official copy-check sees almost none of their text (see unclear_rules). I checked them separately.
7. The registry note's game-wide crushing list and the Crushing page rest on lead-designer Discord quotes from 2023.
8. No wiki page exists for the Voltaic Cannon, Gimbal Roller, Tempest Engine or Safe Firing (the API reports them missing), so the units' own pages were the weapon and ability sources.
